title: Privacy and least privilege
goals: Give each role only needed access

prerequisite.prompt: Does a duration summary need student names to calculate a total?
prerequisite.answer: No; names are not required for that calculation.

vocabulary: Keeping only data needed for the stated purpose
Giving a role only the access it needs
Permission to perform a particular action

blocks.text: A fictional class activity dashboard needs category counts, not names or personal messages. Design its data and role permissions before collection. This exercise uses invented data and policy cards; do not change the Academy's actual authentication settings.

blocks.text: The toy code prints True, False, False. It models a permission decision, not a complete security system. A real server must verify identity and enforce authorization on every protected request; hiding a button in a page is insufficient.

blocks.label: If a student manually requests the review endpoint, should hiding its menu link be enough?

blocks.text: A form asks for names, birthdays and comments to count activity preferences. Remove fields not needed for the purpose. Aggregated counts can still expose information in very small groups; choose reporting rules with the responsible teacher.

Retention must be tied to a purpose and school policy rather than a guessed universal number of days. Identify who can correct or delete records and avoid keeping raw responses indefinitely just because storage is available.

blocks.label: Does the allowed function alone prove an app is secure?

workbook.title: Minimize fields
workbook.prompt: For a count of preferred activities, identify which of activity choice, full name and birthday is necessary.
workbook.answer: Activity choice is needed; full name and birthday are not needed for an anonymous category count.

workbook.title: Trace permissions
workbook.prompt: Under the worked role policy, can teacher read_review and unknown read_summary?

workbook.title: Repair access control
workbook.prompt: A website hides teacher answers using CSS but sends them to student browsers. Explain the flaw and required boundary.
workbook.answer: Students still receive the content. Enforce teacher authorization on the server and do not send answers in student responses.

workbook.title: Design independently
workbook.prompt: Design a fictional preference summary with student and teacher roles. List necessary fields, permitted actions, a retention purpose and a deletion owner.
workbook.answer: Use anonymous choice/count data, student access to approved summary and teacher access only to necessary review data. State a purpose-limited school-approved retention period/process and a responsible deletion owner. Do not collect identifiers without a justified need.

workbook.title: Limit the toy model
workbook.prompt: Does the allowed function alone prove an app is secure?
workbook.answer: No. It omits authentication, server integration, session protection and many other controls; it demonstrates only a policy lookup.
